source: NCERT Class XI, Political Theory, Ch. 8 (Secularism).

sections.heading: 1. What is Secularism?
points: **Secularism** = the principle of **separating religion from the state** and ensuring **freedom and equality for all religions**.
It opposes **religious domination** — of one religion over others, and of religion over other domains of life.
It protects both **inter-religious** and **intra-religious** freedom (against oppression within a religion too).

sections.heading: 2. Why Secularism is Needed
points: To prevent **religious discrimination, persecution and conflict** (communal violence).
To protect **freedom of religion** (including the freedom to not believe) and the rights of **minorities**.
To guard against **intra-religious domination** (e.g. oppression of lower castes, women within a religion).

sections.heading: 3. Western vs Indian Secularism
points: **Western (e.g. American) secularism** — strict **'wall of separation'**: the state neither aids nor interferes with religion; focuses on religion–state separation.

**Indian secularism** — the state maintains a **'principled distance'** from all religions: it can **intervene** in religion to promote equality/reform (e.g. abolishing untouchability, allowing temple entry) and can give **even-handed support** to all religions.
Indian secularism addresses **both inter- and intra-religious** domination and is not strictly anti-religious.

sections.heading: 4. Secularism in the Indian Constitution
points: India is a **secular state** — no official state religion; the word 'secular' was added to the Preamble by the **42nd Amendment (1976)**.
**Fundamental Rights (Art 25–28)** guarantee freedom of religion and equality; the state does not discriminate on religious grounds.
Criticisms of secularism (anti-religious, Western, minority-biased) are addressed by understanding its inclusive Indian form.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Secularism = separation of religion and state + equal freedom for all religions.
Opposes both inter-religious and intra-religious domination.
Western secularism = strict wall of separation; Indian = principled distance (can intervene).
'Secular' added to Preamble by 42nd Amendment (1976).
Freedom of religion = Articles 25–28.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Indian secularism keeps a 'principled distance'** — the state CAN intervene in religion for reform/equality.
**Western secularism = strict separation ('wall')**; Indian is not strict separation.
Indian secularism opposes **both inter- and intra-religious** domination.
The word **'secular' was added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment (1976)**.
